title: Five-star catalogue patterns against the five dots
question: How closely do the fixed five-brightest-catalogue-entry patterns in all 88 IAU constellations match the existing LP2 five-dot geometry under the frozen similarity grid?
reader_question: Do fixed five-star patterns match the five dots?
summary: Volans is closest in the fixed 88-pattern library, with RMS distance 34.9 pixels from LP2-07 dot centres. Orion, Aquila and Bootes rank 69, 72 and 24. Full-selection geometric references sometimes match this closely.
finding: Primary LP2-07: Volans rank 1 of 88, normalized RMS 0.11407900287766708, RMS residual 34.87034651573557 pixels, maximum 55.01971239994527 pixels. Ori/Aql/Boo ranks 69/72/24. Complete-search reference minima are at or below the observed best in 171/4095 uniform-disk and 243/4095 sampled-catalogue queries; plus-one fractions 172/4096 and 244/4096. Dependent LP2-23/56 repetitions also select Volans. All 63360 target registration scores and 264 candidate witnesses independently checked by SVD; all 528 reference counts rechecked.
reader_finding: Volans fits most closely among the 88 fixed five-entry patterns, but still misses the measured dot centres with a typical mismatch of about 35 pixels (RMS). The specified Orion, Aquila and Bootes patterns fit less closely.
reader_limit: This compares one fixed five-brightest-entry rule and projection. It does not identify a constellation, test every asterism or explain a cipher; the other two page appearances repeat the same artwork.
limitations: One exploratory, preselected five-dot query; LP2-23 and LP2-56 are dependent repeats. Five brightest catalogue entries can include close components and do not reproduce every traditional constellation shape. Fixed J2000 gnomonic projection; no proper-motion, epoch, star-subset or projection search. Two geometric reference generators give conditional selection comparisons and Monte Carlo uncertainty, not confirmatory probabilities of astronomical intent. Existing threshold-140 centroids are reused, not independently remeasured.
next_steps: Any different star subset, projection or proposed reading instruction needs a separately frozen rule, appropriate selection references and a reproducible consequence beyond a visual resemblance.

scope.representation: Existing threshold-140 five-dot centroids in original-image pixels, and fixed J2000 gnomonic projections of the five brightest eligible HR entries in each of 88 constellations. Distinct close components retained and flagged.
scope.procedure: After the reviewed synthetic gate and frozen execution-code hashes, fit every correspondence and both orientation branches by exact 2D similarity. Treat LP2-07 as primary, other appearances as dependent robustness. Repeat the whole search for two fixed 4095-query geometric reference generators. Independently check every target score/witness with SVD and recount all saved comparisons.
scope.parameters: 88 candidates × 120 bijections × 2 determinant branches = 21120 labelled registrations per query; translation, arbitrary rotation and positive uniform scale; tie tolerance 1e-12. Three target queries; 4095 uniform-disk queries (PCG64 330120261025) and 4095 within-constellation catalogue-set queries (330120261026). Synthetic gate: 96 math fixtures, 88 exact and 1408 noisy plants; no omitted failures.
scope.exclusions: Other star subsets, traditional line maps, merging close components, proper-motion or epoch tuning, alternative projections, anisotropic scale/shear, star omission, new dot measurements, interpreting repeated artwork as independent evidence, confirmatory astronomy probabilities and decryption.

review.reviewer: Reviewed pretarget scope; independent SVD arithmetic and witness reconstruction; portable full-selection replay and all plant outcomes retained

sources.label: Hoffleit and Warren (1991), Bright Star Catalogue 5th edition, CDS V/50
Official CDS/VizieR catalogue request, exact response retained

visuals.caption: Existing LP2-07 dot centroids (filled) and fitted star entries (open), at the same scale in every panel. Dashes show residuals; no traditional constellation lines are inferred. Volans is the best of the fixed 88 candidates; the other panels show the three named leads.

reproduction.environment: Offline Python 3.12 with NumPy 2.5.4. Frozen catalogue membership/projections/centroids are bundled; no source-cache, image download or network required. Original preparation used Astropy 8.0.2 and the exact lock/install report. Full targets plus 8190 references replay in about 28 seconds on the measured runtime; controls about 8 seconds.

scope_summary: The five dots on LP2-07 against five bright catalogue entries from each of 88 constellations. LP2-23 and LP2-56 check the repeated artwork.
reader_note: About 4% of random disk patterns and 6% of sampled star patterns fit at least this closely after the same search. Those comparisons help put the visual resemblance in context; they do not measure the chance that Cicada intended a constellation.
